newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian gun maker Herstal in shakeup, seeks partner.
newsitem.headline: Belgian gun maker Herstal in shakeup, seeks partner.

text.p: Troubled Belgian arms group Herstal SA, the maker of Browning pistols and Winchester rifles, announced swingeing job cuts but said it still needed to find an industrial partner to survive the next four years.

"The financial needs of the company, which will be around five billion Belgian francs between now and 2000 and only partially met by the sale of the group's stake in Beretta, means we need to find an industrial partner," the company said in a statement late on Tuesday.

"The actual shareholders cannot meet the needs of the group," said Herstal, which is 92-percent owned by loss-making French state defence group GIAT Industries. The remaining shares are held by Belgium's Walloon regional government.
Herstal said it would cut its Belgian workforce of around 1,400 by 395 over the next five years. It would also close a manufacturing facility in Brazil.
"The plan should allow the group as a whole to return to a positive operating profit from 1998," Herstal said.
